digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, V, VI; Mgombato ('mwenjere')
swahili: Mwenjere (shared with Digo, Pakia App. VI); mwengele (Mgombato)

teaser.en: A climber of the grape family that Digo speakers can name by taste alone: its leaves are sour.

summary.en: Mgongolo mlume, also called mwenjere, is a wild climber of the grape family with sour-tasting leaves. Its first name casts it as the 'male' of another plant, mgongolo.

about.en:
*Mgongolo mlume* is a climbing or scrambling plant of the grape family. Like its relatives it holds on with coiled tendrils that grow opposite the leaves. The leaves are divided into several leaflets with toothed edges, and the young stems and leaves often carry sticky glandular hairs. Small greenish flowers grow in flat-topped clusters, and they are followed by small, juicy berries that turn red as they ripen.

Pakia notes that Digo speakers identify it by the look of the whole plant and by the taste of its leaves, which are *kakasi*, sour. It is one of the few wild plants that people recognise mainly by taste.

where.en: It grows over bushes and along thicket and forest edges, scrambling up into other vegetation. The species is widespread in tropical Africa and is common in the coastal bush of Kwale.

culture.en: Pakia uses this plant as his example of the sour taste (*kakasi*) in Digo plant identification. Bitter (*utsungu*) and sweet (*mtswano*) are the other two taste words people use.

names.en: *Mgongolo mlume* means 'male mgongolo'. Pakia records that people see it as the male form of *mgongolo* (*Hoslundia opposita*), though he adds that neither plant has any clear link with *gongolo*, the millipede. Its other name, *mwenjere*, is shared with Swahili, and the Mgombato dictionary lists *mwenjere* as 'type of plant (Cyphostemma adenocaulis)', with Swahili *mwengele*. No English name is recorded.
